newsitem.title: USA: US doesn't want big Japan trade surplus rise--USTR.
newsitem.headline: US doesn't want big Japan trade surplus rise--USTR.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky on Tuesday expressed concern about "disturbing" trends in Japan's trade balance and repeated the United States does not want a big rise in Japan's surplus.

"We have seen some disturbing trends in more recent months in part because of Japan's imposition of a new consumption tax and in part because of a swing in the exchange rate," Barshefsky told the House International Relations Committee.
"We have communicated to Japan we do not expect to see any significant increase in the current account surplus as Japan begins to deregulate its economy," she added.
Barshefsky was testifying on U.S. trade policies. She said some progress has been made in the last four years in opening Japan's markets up to more U.S. goods.
